narrative.summary: Trinidad and Tobago created a Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence in May 2025 and is running a UNESCO-supported AI readiness assessment, but has no national AI strategy or AI law yet. Its binding AI-specific rule is the Judiciary's July 2026 practice direction on the use of generative AI in court proceedings. The national standards body adopted ISO/IEC 42001 on AI management systems as a national standard in 2025, and the 2011 Data Protection Act is only partly in force.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence
Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 and 13 October 2026 from the official gazette and government websites, and every record was checked against its official text. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the digital transformation ministry and the open data portal. The National Digital Transformation Strategy 2024-2027, the AI readiness report and an announced AI governance framework are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Practice Direction on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI)
instruments.english_title: Practice Direction on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI)
instruments.issuing_authority: Chief Justice of Trinidad and Tobago (Judiciary of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago)
instruments.publisher_name: Judiciary of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
instruments.summary: Practice Direction by Chief Justice Ronnie Boodoosingh (dated 7 July 2026) on the use of generative AI in proceedings in the courts of Trinidad and Tobago. Court users may use Gen AI only in limited ways (drafting pleadings, submissions, chronologies, summaries) and must verify every citation and authority; it must not generate the content of affidavits, witness statements or expert opinions, sensitive material must not be put into open tools, and any court document prepared with Gen AI must carry a disclosure certificate naming the tool and version. Judicial officers may use Gen AI for summaries and issue identification but not for reasoning, evidence assessment or editing judgments, and may sanction misuse (striking out, costs, disciplinary action, contempt).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding AI-specific rule set in Trinidad and Tobago; governs Gen AI use by lawyers, litigants, experts and judges.
instruments.current_status: Published as Gazette Notice No. 1013 in the Trinidad and Tobago Gazette Vol. 65 No. 118 of 9 July 2026 (pp. 2148-2153); para. 5 states it comes into effect on 8 July 2026 and continues until superseded; para. 27 says it will be periodically reviewed. Para. 17 notes there is no internal judiciary Gen AI policy at this time.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Gazette No. 118 of 2026 PDF read in full (pdftotext), notice 1013 pp. 2148-2153

instruments.english_title: Data Protection Act, 2011 (Act No. 13 of 2011; Chap. 22:04)
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
instruments.publisher_name: Parliament of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
instruments.summary: General data protection law providing for the protection of personal privacy and information held by public bodies and private enterprises. It sets General Privacy Principles, establishes the Office of the Information Commissioner, and contains specific rules on collection, use, disclosure and data matching of personal information. It has no AI-specific provisions but governs the personal data used to train and run AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Baseline personal-data law that applies to AI processing; only partly in force.
instruments.current_status: Assented to 22 June 2011 and published in Legal Supplement Part A to the Trinidad and Tobago Gazette Vol. 50 No. 83 of 27 June 2011 (the Parliament page also lists 'Published in Gazette on 05-Jan-2012'). Section 1(2) leaves commencement to Presidential Proclamation, and the Ministry of the Attorney General and Legal Affairs revised edition of Chap. 22:04 (unofficial version updated to 31 December 2016) states that Part I and ss. 7-18, 22, 23, 25(1), 26 and 28 came into operation on 6 January 2012 (LN 2/2012), that s. 101 was awaiting proclamation, and lists no commencement for the other provisions (including most of the privacy-principle obligations).
instruments.evidence_reference: curl: Act PDF (gazette legal supplement) read via pdftotext; ttparliament.org Act page (assent 22-Jun-2011); laws.gov.tt revised Chap. 22:04 (updated to 31 Dec 2016) for s. 1(2) commencement note. Status note: Revised edition at laws.gov.tt. Later proclamations were not verified in this review. Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): PDF p.1 header: 'Legal Supplement Part A to the "Trinidad and Tobago Gazette", Vol. 50, No. 83, 27th June, 2011'.

instruments.english_title: Trinidad and Tobago Standard TTS/ISO/IEC 42001:2024, Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Management system
instruments.issuing_authority: Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards
instruments.publisher_name: Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards
instruments.summary: National adoption of ISO/IEC 42001:2024, the AI management system standard, declared a Trinidad and Tobago Standard by the Bureau of Standards under s. 16(4) of the Standards Act, Chap. 82:03. It gives organisations a voluntary framework for establishing, operating and improving an AI management system. The declaration was notified in Legal Notice No. 67 of 2025 together with national adoptions of ISO 20700, ISO 31000, ISO 56001 and ISO/IEC 27001/27002.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National AI management-system standard; voluntary unless a regulator adopts it.
instruments.current_status: Legal Notice No. 67 (Legal Supplement Part B, Vol. 64 No. 33, 25 February 2025; dated 24 February 2025) states the standard was declared with effect from 5 December 2024; the draft (TTS/ISO/IEC 42001:20XX) had been put out for public comment by TTBS, with a virtual stakeholder consultation on 25 September 2024. The standard text itself is sold by TTBS and is not available online.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl: Legal Notice No. 67 of 2025 PDF read in full; TTBS public-comment and stakeholder-consultation pages read. Date note: TTBS declared the standard with effect from 5 December 2024. The declaration notice was dated 24 February 2025 and published in the Legal Supplement on 25 February 2025. Status note: Only the declaration notice was read.

instruments.official_title: Assignment of Responsibility for the Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: Assignment of Responsibility for the Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence (Gazette Notice No. 764 of 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago, acting on the advice of the Prime Minister
instruments.publisher_name: Office of the President of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
instruments.summary: Presidential direction under s. 79(1) of the Constitution assigning Senator Dominic Smith responsibility for the newly named Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence (MPAAI), the first ministry in the country with AI in its remit. The schedule gives it public service administration and modernisation, digital government, digital transformation, ICT policy, strategy and national ICT planning, ICT governance, information and data protection, and oversight of iGovTT and the Telecommunications Authority (TATT). It is the founding act for the ministry that leads national AI policy work, although the schedule does not list AI as a separate business line.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of the lead national AI ministry (MPAAI).
instruments.current_status: Gazette Notice No. 764 in the Trinidad and Tobago Gazette (Extraordinary) Vol. 64 No. 81 of 23 May 2025, dated 12 May 2025 and effective from 12 May 2025. MPAAI's own site states the Ministry of Public Administration and the Ministry of Digital Transformation merged to form MPAAI as of 23 May 2025, citing this Gazette. AI is in the ministry's name but not yet among its formally assigned duties.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl: Gazette No. 81 of 2025 PDF read (pdftotext), notice 764; MPAAI site notice of name change read

leads.title: National Digital Transformation Strategy 2024-2027
leads.english_title: National Digital Transformation Strategy 2024-2027 ('Building Our Lives Digitally')
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transformation (now Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence)
leads.note: Digital strategy with an 'Emerging Technologies' priority that commits to developing national strategies for emerging technologies 'starting with a national Artificial Intelligence (AI) strategy' and an AI sensitisation and capacity-building programme; would be strategy (AI pillar). MPAAI lists it under Publications > General Reports (https://www.mpaai.gov.tt/general-reports/digital-transformation-strategy-2024-2027) but that page carries no download link, and the official open-data listing (data.gov.tt/dataset/national-digital-strategy-2024-2027) was under maintenance on 2026-10-13; the old mdt.gov.tt site is unreachable. Text read only from a non-official copy; no stated publication date found on an official page. Record once the official file and launch date are reachable.

leads.title: National AI Readiness Assessment Report (UNESCO RAM) for Trinidad and Tobago
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence with UNESCO and UNDP
leads.note: MPAAI initiative page (https://www.mpaai.gov.tt/initiatives/ai-readiness-assessment) documents the AILA launch (26 Nov 2025), RAM consultations (Jan 2026) and the national validation workshop (27 Feb 2026); the report itself was not found published on an official site as of 2026-10-13. Would be index-readiness and feed a national AI roadmap/policy.

leads.title: National AI Governance Framework / national AI policy (announced)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence
leads.note: Minister Dominic Smith has publicly said a National AI Governance Framework (data ethics, algorithmic transparency, procurement standards, citizen redress) is being developed; no official document found on mpaai.gov.tt as of 2026-10-13. Announcement of intent only.

leads.title: Artificial Intelligence Bill (reported 2025)
leads.issuing_authority: Parliament of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
leads.note: A third-party AI policy database lists a 2025 AI Bill (statutory AI Authority, deepfake labelling/consent). Searching ttparliament.org for 'artificial', 'deepfake' and AI found no such bill on 2026-10-13; treat as unverified. The opposition's 2026 proposal on AI-misuse penalties also appears to be no tabled bill.

leads.title: Future Ready TT partnership (MPAAI and Ministry of Education) and OpenAI partnership
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence; Ministry of Education
leads.note: Programmes rolling out enterprise generative-AI tools (ChatGPT Enterprise/EDU, Grammarly) in education and the public service (MPAAI media releases Jan and May 2026). Institutional AI-use plans and MoUs, not governance instruments; no published usage guidelines found. Check for any accompanying public-service or school Gen AI usage policy.
